findings.title: Unhandled exceptions from the token exchange and get_user_info produce 500s instead of the error page
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, the outbound calls safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data) (line 423) and get_user_info(payload['access_token']) (line 434) are not wrapped in any error handling. If GitHub is unreachable or returns a connection/timeout error, safe_urlopen raises; if the /user API call fails, get_user_info raises ApiError. Both bubble up as unhandled 500 errors during the installation pipeline, rather than rendering the intended github-integration-failed.html page. The code only gracefully handles the case where the token response parses but lacks access_token. Since this PR's goal is to fail the pipeline cleanly with a friendly error when GitHub cannot complete the OAuth exchange, these calls should be wrapped in try/except and routed to the same error() response.

findings.title: KeyError when Integration metadata has no 'sender' entry
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the new validation reads integration.metadata['sender']['login'] directly. The 'sender' metadata key is only populated in build_integration when state contains sender info (i.e., integrations created from the GitHub installation webhook). Integrations created through the Sentry-initiated install flow, or older integrations created before sender was recorded, do not have this key. If such an Integration row exists without an OrganizationIntegration (e.g., the org link was deleted or is pending deletion) and a user tries to reinstall, this line raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the intended 'Invalid installation request' error page. Use .get() with a fallback (and decide the failure behavior when sender is absent) instead of direct subscripting.

findings.title: No tests for state mismatch or failed token exchange paths
findings.body: The PR description lists three new failure conditions: OAuth user vs installer mismatch, state parameter vs pipeline signature mismatch, and GitHub failing to return an access_token (wrong/reused code). Only the user-mismatch case is tested (test_github_user_mismatch). There is no test that supplies a wrong state parameter to the OAuth callback and asserts the error page, and no test where the access_token response lacks a token (or the /user call returns no login). These are the core security checks being added and regressions in them would currently go undetected.
